content.problemStatement:
Assume you are an awesome parent and want to give your children some cookies. But, you should give each child no more than one cookie.

Each child `i` has a greed factor `g[i]`, which is the smallest size of a cookie that the child will be content with; and each cookie `j` has a size `s[j]`. If `s[j] >= g[i]`, we can assign the cookie `j` to the child `i`, and the child `i` will be content. Your goal is to maximize the number of your content children and output the largest number.

**Example 1:**

```
Input: g = [1,2,3], s = [1,1]
Output: 1
Explanation: You have 3 children and 2 cookies. The greed factors of 3 children are 1, 2, 3. 
And even though you have 2 cookies, since their size is both 1, you could only make the child whose greed factor is 1 content.
You need to output 1.
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: g = [1,2], s = [1,2,3]
Output: 2
Explanation: You have 2 children and 3 cookies. The greed factors of 2 children are 1, 2. 
You have 3 cookies and their sizes are big enough to gratify all of the children, 
You need to output 2.
```

**Constraints:**

* `1 <= g.length <= 30 * 10^4`
* `0 <= s.length <= 30 * 10^4`
* `1 <= g[i], s[j] <= 2^31 - 1`

**Note:** This question is the same as  [2410: Largest Matching of Players With Trainers.](https://leetcode.com/problems/largest-matching-of-players-with-trainers/description/)

notes: Expected output is the JSON-serialised integer returned by findContentChildren.
The greedy exchange argument preserves the maximum possible number of matches.
solution.approach: Sort both arrays and use two pointers. Match the least-greedy remaining child with the smallest cookie that can satisfy that child; otherwise discard the too-small cookie.

better.complexity: O(n log n + m log m) time and O(1) auxiliary space excluding sorting.
better.description: Sort both arrays and greedily match the smallest feasible cookie to the least-greedy child.

optimal.complexity: O(n log n + m log m) time and O(1) auxiliary space excluding sorting.
optimal.description: After sorting, advance the cookie pointer until a cookie can satisfy the current least-greedy child. Match them and advance both pointers; this preserves the maximum number of matches.

bruteForce.description: Enumerate feasible child-cookie assignments and keep the maximum number of satisfied children.

solution.timeComplexity: O(n log n + m log m)
solution.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space excluding sorting implementation

code.Java: class Solution{public int findContentChildren(int[] g,int[] s){Arrays.sort(g);Arrays.sort(s);int i=0,j=0,ans=0;while(i<g.length&&j<s.length){if(s[j]>=g[i]){ans++;i++;j++;}else j++;}return ans;}}

followUps: Why is giving the smallest feasible cookie to the least-greedy child optimal?
What changes if cookies can be reused?
Can counting sort help when the value range is small?
